html:
The Dominion of Newfoundland was a self-governing British dominion on the island of Newfoundland and the Labrador coast, in eastern North America. It is now the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

Norse sailors had camped here around 1000 at L'Anse aux Meadows. From the 1500s European fishing fleets came every summer for the cod of the Grand Banks, and England claimed the island in 1583. Fishing for cod stayed the heart of its economy for four centuries.

Newfoundland governed itself from 1855 and became a dominion in 1907, with the same standing as Canada or Australia. In the First World War its regiment was almost wiped out on the first day of the Battle of the Somme in 1916. Heavy war debt and the Great Depression broke its finances, and in 1934 it became the only dominion to give up self-government, handing power to a commission appointed from London.

After two referendums in 1948, campaigned for by Joey Smallwood, Newfoundland joined Canada in 1949.
sum: The Dominion of Newfoundland was a self-governing British dominion on the island of Newfoundland and the Labrador coast, in eastern North America. It is now the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.
